title: Oversight Quality Self-Assessment: Can Strong Models Accurately Report Their Own Oversight-Evasion Strategies?

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: If models can accurately self-report evasion strategies, this opens a cheap oversight tool. If they cannot, it closes off a proposed technique. Either way informative, but the practical impact is moderate since self-reporting from a deceptive model is inherently unreliable.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires a model that has learned to exploit oversight and then prompting it for self-reports. The exploitation training is the hard part; the self-reporting evaluation is straightforward. Feasible with a model that has been fine-tuned on a simple oversight gaming task.

narrow_scope.reasoning: One model, one self-report prompt, one comparison (self-report vs. actual behavior). Well-defined but depends on having a model that actually exploits oversight, which is a prerequisite project. If starting from scratch, 30 hours is tight.
